provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)

issues.text: The conclusion that the econ-approach is better suited for isolating long-run effects than the epi-approach is not adequately supported; the evaluator believes the authors could do more to back their interpretation.
issues.quote: I believe that the authors could do a bit more to support their interpretation.

issues.text: The econ-approach uses a cross-sectional treatment-intensity measure that may capture other cohort-specific trends unrelated to vaccination, and because it reflects experiences of multiple pre-campaign cohorts it may be poorly suited to a sharp cohort design.
issues.quote: The main concern with the econ-approach is whether this captures other cohort trends unrelated to the disease campaign program

issues.text: The analysis lacks event studies with birth cohort as event time for long-run outcomes, so there is no evidence that cohorts too old to benefit from vaccination did not experience improved outcomes (no cohort pre-trends) and that treatment dynamics are as expected.
issues.quote: Essentially, I would like to see that cohorts too old to benefit from the vaccination campaign did not experience improved long-run outcomes (i.e., no cohort pre-trends)

issues.text: The conceptual difference between mortality rates and infection rates is insufficiently discussed; the two are linked via the fatality rate, and it is unclear why the fatality rate would vary across locations for measles.
issues.quote: Is there any *a priori* reason as to why the fatality rate should vary across locations for a disease such as measles?

issues.text: The description of Acemoglu and Johnson (2007) and Jayachandran et al. (2010) as using the reduced-form cohort-based approach appears inaccurate; these studies compare countries over time or diseases treated with sulfa drugs, not sharp cross-cohort designs. The literature grouping should be clarified.
issues.quote: does not apply this method in a sharp cross-cohort design. They compare countries over time

issues.text: Controlling for survey-year fixed effects instead of age fixed effects may be more intuitive, though the evaluator thinks it uses the same sample variation.
issues.quote: it is perhaps more intuitive controlling for survey-year fixed effects instead of age fixed effects.

issues.text: The rationale for calling Eq. (8) a Bartik-type regression is unclear and needs elaboration.
issues.quote: I am not completely sure why the authors refer to Eq. (8) as a Bartik-type regression. Please elaborate.

issues.text: The paper does not sufficiently discuss whether the epidemiological imputation approach can be applied to other infectious diseases.
issues.quote: The authors could discuss more whether their epidemiological approach can applied to other infectious diseases.
